summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Mark Lehner, an American archaeologist with over 30 years of excavation experience in Egypt. It describes his interdisciplinary method as director of Ancient Egypt Research Associates (AERA), in which specialists examine every excavated object to build a full picture of a site. It also covers his team's Giza Plateau Mapping Project and his identification of Pyramid G1-a as belonging to Hetepheres I.
one_line: American archaeologist Mark Lehner, director of AERA, known for interdisciplinary Giza excavations and the Giza Plateau Mapping Project.
key_facts: Mark Lehner is an American archaeologist with more than 30 years of experience excavating in Egypt.
Mark Lehner was born in North Dakota in 1950.
Mark Lehner is director of Ancient Egypt Research Associates (AERA).
Lehner's approach at AERA is to conduct interdisciplinary archaeological investigation.
Every object excavated by Lehner's team is examined by specialists to create an overall picture of an archaeological site, from the buildings down to the pollen spores.
Lehner's international team currently runs the Giza Plateau Mapping Project.
The Giza Plateau Mapping Project excavates and maps the ancient city of the builders of the Giza pyramid complex.
The ancient city of the Giza pyramid builders dates to the fourth dynasty of Egypt.
Mark Lehner discovered that Pyramid G1-a belonged to Hetepheres I.
Pyramid G1-a is one of the subsidiary pyramids of the Great Pyramid.
Pyramid G1-a was originally thought to belong to Queen Meritites I.
